note: Pinned-SHA benchmark set for the multi-repo QA loop. Every `sha` was resolved with `git ls-remote <url> HEAD` on 2026-08-02 and is a real commit — nothing here is invented. Every `license` is the SPDX id GitHub reports for the repo; NOASSERTION means GitHub could not map the repo's LICENSE to an SPDX id (a custom/source-available licence — check the repo before redistributing anything). `sizeClass` is bucketed from GitHub's reported repo size in KB: small <20MB, medium 20-100MB, large >100MB. The four `groundTruth` rows are the hand-verified edge truths in docs/ground-truth/, which until this harness existed were consumed by nothing.

THIS is the repo docs/ground-truth/spring-petclinic.json describes, in its own first line: spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-microservices, whose compose file is image-only and whose source is found by the inferSourceDir suffix rule. The row originally pointed at spring-projects/spring-petclinic — a different repository (a single-module monolith with no api-gateway, no config-server and none of the 12 hand-verified edges), so the benchmark was scoring a monolith against microservice truth and could only ever report 0%. Sha resolved with `git ls-remote https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-microservices HEAD` on 2026-08-02.

repos.why: Sock Shop is a deployment-only corpus: 22 services run prebuilt images with no readable source in-tree. The correct outcome is an honest zero-file graph with a warning that names deployment-only manifests — not a fabricated architecture. This row exists to catch silent success on image-only repos, the same class as rails (no parser).

repos.why: Ruby has no parser in this engine (only ts/js/py/go/java have grammars). The correct outcome is an honest 'nothing I can read here' — a NoManifestsError, or a graph with essentially no parsed files and a warning that says so. A confident-looking Ruby architecture would be a fabrication and is the failure this row exists to catch.
